page: Amazon Web Services r8idn.large is a memory-optimized virtual server instance built on the AWS Nitro System. The hardware configuration features an Intel x86_64 processor operating at 3.9 GHz, providing 2 dedicated vCPUs across 1 physical core with 2 execution threads. The system provides 16.0 GB of memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per-vCPU ratio that aligns with memory-heavy processing requirements.

Data throughput and local I/O performance are supported by a bundled 118 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume, providing low-latency ephemeral storage directly on the host hardware. Networking capabilities include a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. The instance operates without discrete graphics hardware (0 GPUs) and does not allocate complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

With its 1:8 compute-to-memory configuration combined with local NVMe media, the instance represents an efficient deployment profile for memory-sensitive tasks that require fast scratch space without the overhead of standalone block storage attachments. Primary workload targets include small in-memory databases, caching nodes such as Redis, transient data processing pipelines, and microservices requiring high memory density per vCPU.

The server is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, sustaining an 8 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for memory-heavy operations. The instance features zero GPUs and includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses. With high memory allocation relative to compute cores alongside low-latency local NVMe capacity, r8idn.large provides a balanced footprint for in-memory caching layers, small databases, message queues, and intermediate data processing where fast ephemeral disk I/O and generous memory headroom are essential.
